purpose: Silence expected console.error output in the three DatabaseCleanup API-failure tests via scoped jest.spyOn(console, 'error') with try/finally mockRestore() and spy-call assertions, so the Jest runner output stays clean without masking real failures.
riskRationale: The test-only change is correct and fully verified (17/17 DatabaseCleanup tests, 217/217 suite-wide, ESLint clean). Suppression is scoped strictly to the tests that deliberately trigger the API-failure path, and each spy is restored in a failure-safe try/finally. All console.error spy restoration is now exception-safe across the modified tests, and the .jules/inspector.md entry is correctly dated 2026-07-30. The unrelated composer.lock + vendor/ churn previously carried by this branch has been stripped, leaving only the test + inspector.md + review artifact changes.

text: The core change achieves its goal: console.error is suppressed only in the three tests that intentionally trigger the API-failure path (DatabaseCleanup.js:111/197), the spies are restored in failure-safe try/finally blocks, and assertions verify the error-logging contract in all three tests. All 217 tests pass with ESLint clean, and the .jules/inspector.md entry is correctly dated 2026-07-30. The unrelated composer.lock/vendor churn has been removed from the branch, so the diff now contains only the test + inspector.md + review artifact changes.

reasoning: The console-error silencing change is merge-ready: all three affected tests restore their console.error spy in a failure-safe try/finally, each asserts the error was logged, and the branch no longer carries the unrelated composer.lock/vendor churn. Remaining items are non-blocking: a duplicate whitespace-only commit (a6f2b9cf vs 288db620) that could be squashed for a cleaner history, and the committed review-output.jsonl artifact which could be reverted to master to keep it out of the release ZIP.

message: consoleSpy.mockRestore() is wrapped in try/finally, so the spy is restored even if a waitFor/expect assertion fails — closing the earlier leak where a failed assertion left mockImplementation swallowing console.error for the rest of the suite. This pattern is now applied uniformly to all three console-silencing tests.

All silenced tests now assert the spy actually fired with the expected arguments ('Database cleanup error:', expect.any(Error)), ('Database cleanup error:', {}) for the empty-object rejection, and ('Error fetching database cleanup counts:', expect.any(Error))), so a future refactor that stops logging via console.error fails these tests instead of passing silently — strengthening rather than merely muting the coverage.
Suppression is scoped strictly to the tests that deliberately trigger the API-failure path, leaving genuine console.error output from the rest of the suite visible so real failures are not masked.

The new log entry is dated 2026-07-30 (corrected from the earlier 2024-07-30 copy-paste error), is surrounded by blank lines per markdownlint MD022, and accurately documents the bug, root cause, and the jest.spyOn + mockRestore pattern used, keeping the chronological log coherent.

Commit a6f2b9cf re-sends the same test-file changes as commit 288db620 with the identical message 'test: silence expected console.error logs in DatabaseCleanup tests', differing only in reformatting the two jest.spyOn lines (whitespace-only) with zero functional change — a duplicate commit that adds history noise and complicates revert/bisect.
suggestion: Squash a6f2b9cf into 288db620 (git rebase -i) or drop it so the branch carries a single clean commit for the console-error silencing change.

message: A generated review artifact (review-output.jsonl) is committed at the repo root. It is not excluded in .distignore (only /.jules/ is), so it would ship inside WordPress.org release ZIPs and pollute the plugin package.
